# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I will establish a fixed color code by position: blue, green, red, yellow correspond respectively to four distinct gestures. Deaf can relay this spoken mapping to Blind, allowing the manual instructions to be transmitted safely in the next round.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎", "👌", "🤟"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please read the manual and tell me exactly what condition determines the safe wire. Also relay the Deaf's visual findings to me.
Deaf says to Mute: Use this code for your next answer: 👍 means wire 1, 👎 means wire 2, 👌 means wire 3, and 🤟 means the manual requires more tactile information. Consult the manual for display 0, red light, and wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. Send exactly the applicable gesture or 🤟.

The manual says a red light requires cutting the green wire. Deaf has identified wire 2 as green and explicitly defined 👎 as wire 2, so I should transmit only that gesture.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: The Deaf's four code symbols were not perceptible to me. Please relay the manual's exact rule and any needed code through an available channel.

Blind needs the manual rule and the gesture-to-wire code, but cannot perceive gestures. Deaf is the only available relay: I will send the established code sequence again, along with the applicable wire indication, so Deaf can state both aloud to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎", "👌", "🤟", "👎"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | yellow |
| red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Deaf says to Mute: New bomb state: display 0, blue light, wire 1 yellow, wire 2 already CUT, wire 3 red. On your next turn, read the manual and speak the exact required action directly to Blind. If it depends on tactile controls, first state that dependency and do not guess.

The blue-light rule requires cutting the red wire. Wire 3 is red, while wire 2 is already cut; under the established code, wire 3 is 👌. I cannot speak to Blind, so I will send Deaf the exact gesture for Deaf to relay.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌"])
```

TURN 5

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|

| red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: The correct cut was accepted. I have no new tactile control details shown yet; please provide the manual's next instruction and tell me what tactile fact you need.

The manual’s applicable rule is still blue light → cut the red wire, but the current bomb state has not been provided after the accepted cut. I need Blind to report which intact wire is red, or any tactile control that determines the wire, before naming an action. I will signal Deaf to relay that dependency.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
```

DEFUSAL MANUAL:

|---|---|

System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Deaf says to Mute: New state: display 0, green light; wire 1 yellow remains, wires 2 and 3 are CUT. Your 🤟 code means tactile information is required. Ask Blind for the relevant tactile details, consult the manual, and speak the exact action to Blind. Do not guess.

The green-light rule requires cutting the yellow wire. Deaf reports that wire 1 is yellow and remains intact, while wires 2 and 3 are already cut, so no further tactile fact is needed: Blind should cut wire 1. I will send Deaf the established wire-1 signal to relay verbally.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

The current green-light rule requires cutting the yellow wire. Deaf reported that wire 1 is yellow and still intact, so Blind should cut wire 1; no additional tactile condition is needed. I will signal Deaf with the established wire-1 code so Deaf can speak the action to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```
